items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: And after '53, Johnny Griffin come out of the service, and we had a job down at the Bludnote. I was with Ella -- it was Johnny Griffin, and Babs, Wilbur Campbell Camel, George Freeman...

ctx.x: Well maybe, the one or two occasions when something did happen, brought that attitude on, like the record with Art Blakey, where Spanky played, in Harlem on My Mind the one ... there's a picture of it -- the one with Sam Dockery.

Yeah, that was on Atlantic. Johnny Griffin joined the Messengers, and it was Art Blakey and the Messengers, with Thelonious. Now I was supposed to play on part of it, and the Messengers -- Bill Hardman -- and I was out with Wilbur Campbell, and I got drunk on top of it, too. And we got down to the studio, I go in the bathroom and pass out. See, and whoever the date was, they though Monk was gonna do the same thing, so they had Sam Dockery on a standby basis. So I missed that date.

Well, it's all a part of the…
The period after you had gotten sick and the band broke up, you went back with Miles -- and then what did you do?

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: The name 'Johnny Junior Mance Campbell' appears only in the metadata/note field '[(note)] Thelonious Himself Johnny Junior Mance Campbell' and is not mentioned in the interviewee's spoken transcript.

ctx.x: And Monk called me up just to play on one track of his Thelonious's album, his solo album. And about this time, Johnnie Griffin was in New York; Jimmy Mann was there working, and Wilbur Camel came out from Chicago, so Keepnews people said, 'well, it's time for your own ...' he didn't call me until Lionel phoned me; he got word to me, and he say, 'You got a date tomorrow', and I said, 'My date? I got no material.' And he said, 'Well, you be in the studio at such and such a time.'
Thelonious Himself Johnny Junior Mance Campbell
Wilbur, 'cause I didn't have a phone
